questions.explain: A nonclustered columnstore index sits on a rowstore table, so OLTP keeps rowstore performance while analytical queries use the columnstore copy — the chapter's HTAP pattern.
options: Clustered columnstore: the table becomes the columnstore and OLTP rows are converted
Nonclustered columnstore: a secondary index on the rowstore table, letting OLTP and analytics share one database
Two separate databases synchronized by replication
A columnstore index on a readable AG secondary only
questions.q: Which columnstore flavor is the chapter's HTAP pattern — one database serving both OLTP and analytics?

questions.explain: The chapter says to aim for ~1M rows per compressed rowgroup and to check rowgroup health with sys.column_store_row_groups, because trickle loads create small, inefficient rowgroups.
options: 10,000 rows per rowgroup
100,000 rows per rowgroup
Delete all rowgroups under 1M rows nightly
~1M rows per compressed rowgroup, checked via sys.column_store_row_groups
questions.q: What is the chapter's guidance for columnstore rowgroup health?

questions.explain: CDC asynchronously captures inserted, updated, and deleted rows with full before/after images (the analytics feeder), while Change Tracking synchronously records only which rows changed — ideal for syncing caches.
options: CDC captures full before/after images for ETL; Change Tracking records only which rows changed
Change Tracking captures before/after images; CDC records only changed row IDs
Both do the same thing; CDC is just newer
CDC is synchronous and Change Tracking is asynchronous
questions.q: How do CDC and Change Tracking differ as pipeline feeders?

questions.explain: The default is columnstore in-engine — one system, one security model, real-time data. Offload when the analytics resource profile (bursty, massive, team-separate) conflicts with OLTP stability.
options: Always offload to a cloud data warehouse
Default to in-engine columnstore; offload only when the analytics workload's resource profile conflicts with OLTP stability
Offload everything to a lakehouse for cost
Never run analytics on SQL Server
questions.q: What is the chapter's default decision on in-engine analytics versus offload?

questions.explain: Columnstore loves memory and batch mode wants generous memory grants, so workload groups limiting analytics memory/CPU protect OLTP — an unbounded dashboard query must never take down order entry.
options: Disabling batch mode execution
Resource governance (workload groups) limiting analytics memory/CPU so OLTP is protected
Running analytics only on the primary
Turning off compression
questions.q: How should a DBA protect the OLTP workload when analytics share the same engine?

title: Chapter 22: SQL Server Analytics: Columnstore and Workload Offload
